criteria.text: `GET /api/compare?a=lula&b=bolsonaro` (defaults otherwise) returns 200 with a body of exactly `{ days, a: { person, about }, b: { person, about }, terms }` — no `links`, `signature`, `nodes` or `outlets` keys.
`a.person` and `b.person` are each `{ id, name, aliases }`, matching the row in `persons` for that id.
`GET /api/compare?a=nobody&b=lula` and `GET /api/compare?a=lula&b=nobody` both return 404 with body `{ "error": "person not found" }`.
`GET /api/compare` with `a`/`b` omitted returns 404 with the same body.
`a.about` for `a=lula` at a given `days`/`source`/`domain`/`lean` equals `graphFor(lula, sameQuery).stats.about` — proving `about` is unfiltered by term/kind and matches `/graph`'s existing meaning.

A term present in the fixture only for `lula` (e.g. "reforma tributária", `days: 30`) appears in the response with a real `{ count, pmi, tone }` object under `a` and `null` under `b` — not omitted from `terms`, not a `{ count: 0, ... }` object.
Symmetrically, a term that only `tarcisio`'s docs carry appears with a real figure on that side and `null` on the other when compared against a person whose docs never mention it.

A term equal to (or containing) one side's own name word — e.g. the term "lula" when `a=lula` — reads `"name"` under `a`. If that same term is genuine vocabulary for `b` (has doc_terms rows about `b` outside `b`'s own name), it reads a real `{ count, pmi, tone }` object under `b` in the same response.

For a `(term, kind)` present in `graphFor(lula, q).nodes` (an overlapping query scope), `/api/compare?a=lula&b=...`'s `a` figure for that same term has the identical `count`, `pmi` and `tone` as the `/graph` node — proving the per-side computation reuses the same formula and the same shared PMI universe.
`GET /api/compare?a=lula&b=lula` returns, for every term, an identical value under `a` and `b` (deep-equal), including `"name"` entries.
`limit=1` still returns more than one term when both the count-ranked and pmi-ranked top-1 differ per side (up to 4 distinct keys unioned) — proving both selection criteria are applied, not just one.
`terms` is ordered by `term` asc, then `kind` asc.
An out-of-window query (`days=1`, scoped so neither person has a doc that recent) returns `terms: []` and `about: 0` on both sides, not an error.

`GET /api/compare` appears in the cache-control test's rolling-window list (`s-maxage` matching the existing `ROLLING` tier) and its 404s return `no-store` — both already implied by `src/cache.ts`'s existing `tierOf` logic (the last path segment `compare` is not in `TREND`, so no `src/cache.ts` change is needed; only the test list grows).

`docs/api.md` names the `/api/compare` route, its `a`/`b` parameters, and states that a term absent from one side's figures is distinguishable in the payload from a term hidden as that side's own name (checked against `docsText`, never against one page's heading or wording).
